A rejected DELETE (e.g., server error or network failure) would result in an unhandled promise rejection with no user feedback, leaving the row in place silently. The mechanism described is verifiable from the diff, though it is an error-path issue rather than a mainline behavior defect, so confidence is moderate.

judged_text: The delete action chains destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so any rejected DELETE — the 500 the server returns for a stale id, a network failure, or a permission error — becomes an unhandled promise rejection that is never surfaced. An admin who confirms deletion of a host that was already deleted elsewhere, or whose request fails, sees the row remain with no error dialog at all and no console-visible feedback in the UI; the same component guards save() with .catch(popupAjaxError), so this is a silently swallowed failure on a user-facing operation, not a UX choice.
